sections.description: one test suite the coverage and mutation sensors run, found by its name; its first key creates it

keys.description: the language of the suite, which decides how its coverage report is read
the folder the suite runs from, relative to the repository
the command that runs the suite and writes its coverage report, run in the user's login shell
a line that makes the suite's tools available in a fresh login shell, such as a virtual environment or a Node version manager
the test runner of a typescript suite; no other language takes one
one environment variable the suite runs with
the coverage report the suite writes, relative to the suite's directory; * matches a folder or file name
the format of the coverage report the suite writes
the C.R.A.P. score above which a function is reported, above 0; default 30
where the sensor writes its overlay, relative to the repository; default .recognizer/cache/overlays/crap.json
untracked repository paths Mutation copies into its working copy, such as a virtual environment or node_modules
the time budget of a Mutation run in minutes, above 0; a run that reaches it stops and keeps what it measured
keys.default_text: no time budget: the run continues until it finishes

keys.description: the most mutants tested at once, at least 1
keys.default_text: sized from the machine's cores and free memory

keys.description: how many times a mutant may run longer than the unmutated suite before it counts as timed out, above 0; default 10
whether a run measures only what changed since the last record; default true
where the sensor keeps what it has measured, relative to the repository; default .recognizer/cache/mutation/record.json
where the sensor writes the mutants that survived, relative to the repository; default .recognizer/cache/mutation/survivors.json
where the sensor writes its overlay, relative to the repository; default .recognizer/cache/overlays/mutation.json
turns the default threshold of a metric off
a finding when the metric is above this value; a metric takes above or below, not both
a finding when the metric is below this value; a metric takes above or below, not both
how a finding of the metric is reported; default warning
